subject.title: fix(cron): support current and session: targets in initial delivery resolution

question: Should `current` and `session:*` cron jobs continue using the persistent-session contract with delivery left implicit at creation, or should OpenClaw intentionally persist announce delivery for those targets?
rationale: The merged persistent-session restoration distinguishes these targets from detached `isolated` jobs, while this PR interprets shared validation and runtime fallback checks as requiring identical persisted defaults; that product-contract choice cannot be inferred safely from helper consistency alone.

options.title: Preserve persistent-session semantics
options.body: Keep `resolveInitialCronDelivery` isolated-only and require a real failing current-main execution path before changing the delivery boundary.

options.title: Redefine the stored default
options.body: Approve persisted announce for persistent targets only with explicit upgrade intent and end-to-end proof that each job produces exactly one correctly routed user-visible result.

recommendation.title: Preserve persistent-session semantics
recommendation.body: Keep `resolveInitialCronDelivery` isolated-only and require a real failing current-main execution path before changing the delivery boundary.

likelyOwner.reason: The most directly relevant product contract was established through the persistent-session restoration authored and merged under this person's direction.
